note: Spike #112: scoping spike for runtime spectral decomposition in srmech. Lift offline encoder-to-bit-exact-spectral-file workflow onto a runtime callable + tool-schema surface, with biology-inspired delta encoding so unchanged-state cost is sublinear. Design-not-implementation; output is class-chain map + tool-schema surface sketch + follow-up spike list.
primitive_chain_target: Class M (HDC bind / unbind / bundle / similarity)

note: Five spectral notebooks (antikythera / ephemerides / chess / othello / logo / mfo) all use OFFLINE encoders producing bit-exact spectral files (NDJSON or JSON-on-disk). srmech currently exposes the primitive operations (Class L laplacian / hermitian_eigendecompose / matvec; Class M bind/bundle/permute/similarity; Class C cascade; Class I cyclic; Class K asymptotic-DOF). No srmech.spectral.* namespace exists. tool_schema.register_tool() is the established discovery surface; ~87 ToolEntry registrations covering srmech.amsc.* + srmech.qm.*. Runtime spectral decomposition is a COMPOSITION of existing primitives, not a new class.

canonical_ssot: Rao & Ballard (1999) Nat Neurosci 2(1):79-87. Friston (2010) Nat Rev Neurosci 11(2):127-138 (free-energy principle).
citation_method: cite-by-ref (paywalled); Friston 2010 also cited in srmech Spike #46 round1_references.ndjson
mechanism: Cortex propagates prediction errors upward, not full sensory state. Higher layers maintain generative model; only the residual (observation minus prediction) is encoded at each ascending level. Equivalent to delta encoding against a learned reference.
framework_mapping: Class C (cascade-orientation; the directed prediction-flow) composed with Class L (eigenbasis as the generative-model reference). prediction_error_spectrum = U^T (state_observed - state_predicted). Identity-form: prediction-error IS a Class L matvec on a state-delta vector.
tractability: TRACTABLE in Phase C1 vocabulary; no new primitive needed. Existing dense_matvec_complex (Class L) handles the matvec; cascade-direction is Class C semantics on chain ordering.

canonical_ssot: Olshausen & Field (1996) Nature 381(6583):607-609; Olshausen & Field (1997) Vision Res 37(23):3311-3325 (overcomplete basis derivation).
citation_method: cite-by-ref (Nature paywall); arXiv-equivalent NOT available (1996 pre-arXiv-ubiquity)
mechanism: V1 simple cells form an overcomplete basis where natural-image statistics produce sparse activation: only a small subset of basis functions has non-zero coefficient for any given image. Truncation of small coefficients is asymptotically lossless on natural-image manifold.
framework_mapping: Class K (asymptotic-DOF; truncate at the rate-of-approach to the sparse asymptote, NOT at a fixed cardinality). Class L gives the basis (eigenbasis of substrate Laplacian); Class K decides where to cut the spectrum. K's pin-slot mechanism IS the sparse-truncation discipline.
tractability: TRACTABLE; Class K already in v0.4.0+ via Phase C1 rc7 (asymptotic_dof + pin_slot primitives). Sparse-truncation needs a new Class K op spike #117 — call it sparse_truncate(coeffs, asymptote_rate) — but no new class.

canonical_ssot: Church et al. (2011) Genome Res 21(11):1856-1865 (hg19 reference); GRCh38 documentation (Genome Reference Consortium, 2013).
citation_method: cite-by-ref (paywalled refs; GRCh38 reference is open-source documentation)
mechanism: Clinical genomics stores VCF (variant call format) deltas against a reference genome (e.g. hg38). Full genome reconstructible from delta + reference. Storage cost scales with variant count (~3M SNVs per human), not genome length (~3G bases).
framework_mapping: DIRECT match to chess-spectral §5b's rank-1 delta identity. Reference state + change-list = full state. Class M bind operation is the algebraic delta primitive: bind(reference, current) = delta_handle; bind(reference, delta_handle) = current (self-inverse property).
framework_class_chain: Class M (bind / unbind via self-inverse XOR)
tractability: TRACTABLE; Class M hdc.bind IS the delta operation. Spike #114 candidate: formalise hdc.bind as the canonical delta-encoding primitive with reference-handle + delta-handle semantics.

canonical_ssot: Findlay & Walker (1999) Behav Brain Sci 22(4):661-721 (saccade control model); Curcio et al. (1990) J Comp Neurol 292(4):497-523 (foveal cone density).
mechanism: Eye samples high-information regions at fovea (high cone density, ~5 deg arc) and low-information periphery at lower resolution. Only the foveal patch gets fully encoded; rest is gist + saliency map. Information density follows the data, not the geometry.
framework_mapping: Region-of-interest spectral encoding; full eigenbasis decomposition on changed/high-saliency patches, coarse coefficients elsewhere. Class L sub-Laplacian on a submask. Identity-form: foveal-encoding IS a localized Class L decomposition restricted to a region-of-attention.
tractability: TRACTABLE but requires a new sub-op of Class L: region_restricted_laplacian(state, mask). Spike #119 candidate (lower priority).

canonical_ssot: Lisman & Grace (2005) Neuron 46(5):703-713 (hippocampal-VTA novelty loop); Kumaran & Maguire (2007) Hippocampus 17(9):735-748 (novelty-vs-familiarity).
mechanism: CA1 acts as a comparator: predicted state from CA3 vs observed sensory input. Novelty signal triggers consolidation; routine inputs are filtered out. Functionally equivalent to predictive-coding's error-only-propagation with an additional gating threshold.
framework_mapping: Composes with predictive_coding: prediction_error_spectrum thresholded by a Class K asymptotic-DOF gate (rate-of-change of prediction-error magnitude). Below-threshold = familiar = no update; above-threshold = novel = full re-encode.
tractability: TRACTABLE as composition; same primitives as predictive_coding + a gating sub-op.

canonical_ssot: Thompson & Spencer (1966) Psychol Rev 73(1):16-43; Rankin et al. (2009) Neurobiol Learn Mem 92(2):135-138 (revised criteria).
mechanism: Repeated stimuli produce decreasing response amplitude as receptor populations adapt. Equivalent to per-mode confidence weighting: stable modes get lower update gain; novel modes get higher update gain.
framework_mapping: Per-coefficient learning-rate decay on the spectral state. Class N continued-fraction convergent semantics — confidence accumulates as continued-fraction convergents stabilise. Identity-form: habituation IS a Class N convergent reading on per-coefficient stability.
tractability: TRACTABLE; Class N already in v0.4.0+ via Phase C1 rc8 (rational.py convergents). Needs a new op: per_coefficient_stability(coefficient_history). Spike #120 candidate (lower priority).

citation_method: cite-by-ref (PNAS; freely accessible historically but cite the journal record)
mechanism: Pattern completion via energy descent on a recurrent network. Stored patterns are eigenvectors of the synaptic matrix; novel input descends to nearest stored attractor. Delta from attractor is the encoded content; the attractor itself is the reference.
framework_mapping: Hopfield is structurally Class L (graph Laplacian / Hermitian operator) + Class C (gradient-descent cascade). The 'stored pattern' is a low-energy eigenvector; encoding-as-delta-from-attractor is exactly the rank-1 delta identity from chess-spectral §5b. NOT a new operation; instantiates existing class chain.
tractability: TRACTABLE as composition of existing primitives.

canonical_ssot: Kanerva (2009) Cognitive Computation 1:139-159; Plate (1995) IEEE TNN 6(3):623-641 (HRR).
citation_method: cite-by-ref (paywalled; Kanerva 2009 also cited in srmech.amsc.hdc module docstring per Phase C1)
mechanism: Bind / unbind / bundle / permute on high-dimensional binary vectors. Bind is self-inverse XOR; therefore bind(reference, current) = delta naturally; bind(reference, delta) = current. Compositional, noise-tolerant, sublinear delta cost.
framework_mapping: Already Class M in srmech.amsc.hdc (v0.4.0 rc8). HDC bind IS the delta-encoding primitive in the existing vocabulary. NOT new; just under-utilised for runtime spectral.
tractability: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED in C/Python parity per Phase C1 rc8.

decision: srmech.spectral as a NEW LIGHTWEIGHT NAMESPACE composing existing primitives
rationale: Per [[feedback_no_privileged_primitive_classes]] and [[user_stance_identity_not_implementation_discipline]], runtime spectral decomposition IS a composition of Classes L/M/C/K/N, not a new primitive class. srmech.spectral is a thin convenience layer that registers tool-schema entries on top of the existing srmech.amsc.* primitives and provides handle-based state management for delta encoding. No new class, no new C primitive (operations route through existing libsrmech symbols).
alternative_considered: Add to srmech.amsc.* as a new module — REJECTED because amsc is the AMSC framework + primitive-class home; spectral runtime is a layered consumer of amsc primitives, not itself a primitive class.
alternative_considered_2: Add to srmech.qm.* — REJECTED because qm is canonical QM/QFT/SM physics layer; spectral runtime is substrate-agnostic (image, chess, ephemeris, gear-DAG) so doesn't belong in qm.

ops.name: srmech.spectral.decompose
ops.signature: decompose(state: bytes | numpy_array, substrate_descriptor: SpectralSubstrate) -> SpectralHandle
ops.summary: Full eigenbasis decomposition of state on substrate's Laplacian. Returns handle carrying (eigenbasis_U, coefficients, substrate_id, content_sha256).

ops.name: srmech.spectral.delta
ops.signature: delta(reference: SpectralHandle, new_state: bytes | numpy_array) -> SpectralDelta
primitives_used: Class M (bind for binary states; matvec on (new - old) for numeric)
Class L (sparse U^T row selection per chess-spectral §5b)
ops.summary: Rank-k delta from reference state. If states differ at k positions, returns k weighted eigenbasis rows (NOT a full decomposition). Cost is O(k * n) instead of O(n^2).

ops.name: srmech.spectral.recompose
ops.signature: recompose(handle: SpectralHandle, deltas: list[SpectralDelta] = ()) -> bytes | numpy_array
ops.summary: Reconstruct state from base handle + optional delta stack. Cost is linear in (n + sum(k_i)).

ops.name: srmech.spectral.predict
ops.summary: Predictive-coding (Friston 2010) — extrapolate future spectral state via cascade. Used as reference for prediction_error encoding.

ops.name: srmech.spectral.prediction_error
ops.signature: prediction_error(predicted: SpectralHandle, observed_state: bytes | numpy_array, threshold: float = 0.0) -> SpectralDelta | None
ops.summary: Rao-Ballard / Friston error spectrum. Returns None if below novelty threshold (hippocampal-gate semantics); otherwise returns the residual spectrum.

ops.name: srmech.spectral.truncate_sparse
ops.summary: Olshausen-Field sparse truncation — drop modes whose contribution falls below the asymptotic-DOF rate. NOT a fixed-cardinality cut; the cut is at the rate-of-approach.

ops.name: srmech.spectral.similarity
ops.summary: Compare two spectral handles. Used for caching / deduplication / novelty detection.

rationale: The substrate carries the Laplacian (chess 8x8 grid; ephemeris body-coupling graph; image pixel-neighbour grid; gear DAG; LOGO turtle graph). Substrate is the FIBER (per [[user_stance_fiber_as_spatially_absent_encoding]]) — algebraic content spatially-absent until projected by the state. The descriptor is the AMSC-attested specification of the substrate; eigenbasis is computed once and cached by content_sha256.
fields: attestation (MPR v1 block per srmech AMSC)

ssot: chess-spectral notebook §5b 'Value × Position factorization'; rank-1 perturbation identity Δf̂ = -v · U^T δ_k = -v · U[k,:]; verified reconstruction error 9.29e-17 (machine zero).
mechanism: When state changes at k positions with delta-values v_i, spectral delta is sum over (i in changed_positions) of v_i * U[i, :]. Cost is O(k * n) reads on U, not O(n^2). For chess (k=1 typical per ply), this is O(n) = O(64). For an image of n pixels with k changing, k can be tiny (a video frame's moving pixels).
framework_class_chain: Class M (bind/unbind for binary state encodings)

rationale: Computing the eigenbasis of a Laplacian is expensive (Jacobi O(n^3) at small n; n<=256 in libsrmech native bound). When the substrate is fixed (chess board, ephemeris coupling graph), the eigenbasis is identical across all states on that substrate. Cache by substrate's content_sha256 per srmech AMSC discipline; reuse across all decompose / delta calls on that substrate.
tool_schema_integration: Caching is internal; not exposed in tool_schema (introduces no new public op)

registration_path: srmech.spectral.__init__ calls register_tool() at module import; entries carry summary + parameter-shape + smoke_test_hint per existing ToolEntry contract

tractable_in_phase_c1: delta (Class L row-select + Class M bind)
default_per_feedback_no_privileged: All new ops dissolve into existing classes A-N as sub-operations; vocabulary stays at 14.

principle_per_feedback_no_binding_layer_: Every primitive earns its C surface; spectral-namespace operations route through existing libsrmech symbols (srmech_dense_laplacian, srmech_hermitian_eigendecompose, srmech_hdc_bind/unbind/bundle/similarity).
new_libsrmech_symbols_needed: srmech_l_row_select_matvec (Class L sub-op for rank-k delta efficient path)

title: Predictive-coding cascade design — Class C ∘ Class L composition for prediction-error spectra
scope: Design + implement srmech.spectral.predict and srmech.spectral.prediction_error. Class C cascade orientation drives Class L eigenbasis time-evolution; prediction error is U^T (observed - predicted). Hippocampal gating is Class K asymptotic-DOF threshold. Implementation: new Class C sub-op srmech_c_cascade_extrapolate; new Class K sub-op srmech_k_novelty_gate.

title: HDC bind/unbind as delta-encoding primitive — formalise reference-handle + delta-handle semantics
scope: Document Class M hdc.bind as the canonical delta-encoding primitive. Add srmech.spectral.delta as a thin wrapper. Confirm rank-k delta identity for binary-state substrates (board games, occupancy maps) where rank-1 chess identity holds bit-exact. Demonstration substrate: chess-spectral ply-delta from §5b. New Class L sub-op: srmech_l_row_select_matvec for efficient rank-k delta on numeric states.
estimated_effort: 1 substantive spike (counterpoint on chess + ephemerides) + 1 rc

title: Tool-schema surface design for runtime spectral — register 7 srmech.spectral.* ToolEntry registrations
scope: Per srmech.amsc.tool_schema discipline (Task #198, ~87 existing entries), add 7 ToolEntry registrations for srmech.spectral.{decompose, delta, recompose, predict, prediction_error, truncate_sparse, similarity}. Include parameter shape, smoke_test_hint, example, owner='srmech', category='spectral'. Run tool_schema validation tests in pytest. Document the runtime-spectral discovery surface so LLM-side tool-callers can invoke it.

title: Chess-spectral ply-delta as cross-substrate template — instantiate rank-1 identity across image / ephemeris / gear-DAG / sensor stream
scope: Empirical demonstration that the chess-spectral §5b rank-1 identity (Δf̂ = -v · U^T δ_k; reconstruction error 9e-17) generalises across substrates. Test substrates: (a) image pixel-change delta (n=64x64 patch); (b) ephemeris one-body position update (n=52 bodies in ephemerides-spectral); (c) Antikythera gear DAG one-tooth-count perturbation (n=number of gears); (d) LOGO turtle one-step delta. For each: confirm reconstruction error at machine precision. This validates substrate-agnostic claim of the runtime-spectral API.
primary_class_chain: Class L (substrate-agnostic application of rank-k delta identity)
ssot: MPR v1 attestation per spectral file

title: Sparse-coding (Class K) as compression / truncation discipline — Olshausen-Field rate-based cut
scope: Implement srmech.spectral.truncate_sparse using Class K asymptotic-DOF (Spike #111 + Spike #105.K precedent). Cut spectral coefficients at the rate-of-approach to the sparse asymptote, NOT at a fixed cardinality. The rate-of-approach IS the natural-image / chess-position / ephemeris-state truncation discipline — biology already picked this answer (V1 sparse code). New Class K sub-op: srmech_k_sparse_truncate(coeffs, asymptote_rate). Compare to fixed-cardinality cuts on a test corpus.

title: Region-restricted Laplacian — saccadic-foveal-density encoding for high-resolution local + low-resolution global
scope: Lower priority. Add Class L sub-op region_restricted_laplacian(state, mask) for spatially-non-uniform encoding density (high-information regions get full eigenbasis; rest get coarse). Maps to saccadic eye movement biology. Class L sub-op, not a new class.

title: Habituation via Class N convergents — per-coefficient stability semantics for streaming spectral
scope: Lower priority. Use Class N continued-fraction convergents to track per-coefficient stability over time. Stable coefficients get low update gain (habituated); novel ones get high gain. Maps to receptor-desensitisation biology. Class N sub-op, not a new class.

note: No biology strategy in survey requires a NEW PRIMITIVE CLASS outside A-N. All map cleanly as compositions or sub-ops within Classes L/M/C/K/N. Per [[feedback_no_privileged_primitive_classes]] default-dissolve discipline, vocabulary stays at 14. The runtime-spectral capability IS class-operator composition per [[user_stance_identity_not_implementation_discipline]] — not implements.
math_doesnt_lie_check: rank-1 delta identity is proved bit-exact in chess-spectral §5b (recon error 9.29e-17, machine zero); identity generalises to substrate-agnostic claim because U is unitary on any Hermitian Laplacian; the algebra works across substrates by construction.
